seo.title: Bathroom Survey in Gerrards Cross | £125 Fixed-Price Survey | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: Book a £125 bathroom survey in Gerrards Cross. We measure the room, check waste runs and access, and scope the job properly before any installation quote.

hero.intro: Before we quote for a bathroom installation anywhere in Gerrards Cross, we carry out a fixed-price £125 survey at the property. It's the stage where a floor plan and a wish list meet the reality of your walls, your waste runs and your access routes, and it's what stops a quote turning into a list of surprises once the fitting team is on site. Gerrards Cross is an affluent Buckinghamshire commuter village close to Beaconsfield and Chalfont St Peter, and it's around 25 to 30 minutes by road from our base in Bracknell — close enough that we survey here regularly, without it being a detour from how we normally work. Property investment tends to run deep in a village like this, and a bathroom refurbishment is often one part of a longer-term plan for the house rather than a quick, one-off fix, which is exactly why getting the survey right at the outset matters.

sections.heading: What the £125 survey covers
sections.body: The survey fee is fixed at £125 regardless of the size or complexity of the room, and it's deducted from your project cost if you go ahead with an installation. On the day, we measure the room accurately, identify where the waste pipe currently runs and whether it can realistically be moved, check the water supply and pressure feeding the room, and look at the floor and wall build-up to establish what's underneath the surfaces you can see. We also check access — door widths, staircases, and how materials will move in and waste will move out — because that affects both the practicality of the work and, in some cases, the fittings you can realistically choose. By the end of the survey you get a written scope and a firm quote, not a ballpark figure that moves once work starts. We don't ask for a deposit to book the survey conversation itself; it's a paid, fixed-fee visit precisely so the advice you get is based on your actual property in Gerrards Cross, not a generic estimate drawn up from a distance.

sections.heading: What that looks like in a typical Gerrards Cross property
sections.body: Gerrards Cross sits in the affluent Buckinghamshire commuter belt, close to Beaconsfield and Chalfont St Peter, and it's the kind of village where a bathroom is rarely treated as an afterthought — homeowners here tend to be investing in a property they plan to stay in and improve properly, rather than fitting the cheapest option that will do for now. At survey, that generally translates into a conversation about getting the specification right the first time: how a reconfigured layout, a wet room conversion, or a higher-specification finish will actually work in your particular room, rather than assuming a standard off-the-shelf layout will do. Being around 25 to 30 minutes from our Bracknell base also means we're not squeezing a Gerrards Cross survey in as an outlier — it's a normal part of our working area, which matters when it comes to scheduling the survey itself and, later, the fitting team's time on site. Whatever the age or layout of your particular house, the survey is where we confirm the waste run, the water supply, the floor and wall build-up, and the access route specifically for your property, rather than working from assumptions about the area.

sections.heading: Booking your survey
sections.body: If you're planning a bathroom installation in Gerrards Cross, the survey is the sensible first step whether you already have a design in mind or you're still working out what's possible in the space. We'll come to the property, take the measurements and checks above, and talk through what you're hoping to achieve — whether that's a full reconfiguration, a wet room conversion, or simply replacing an existing layout with a higher specification. You'll leave the visit with a clear, written scope and a fixed quote for the installation, so you can compare it properly against anything else you're considering, without having to guess at extra costs that might appear later. We fit only — the survey covers what we need to install your bathroom to the specification you've chosen, and we work from your own supplied products or alongside your showroom or designer.

faqs.q: Does the £125 survey fee come off the final price?
faqs.a: Yes. The £125 is a fixed fee for the visit itself, and it's deducted from your total project cost if you go ahead with an installation through us.

faqs.q: Do I need a design ready before you survey my Gerrards Cross property?
faqs.a: No. Some of the Gerrards Cross properties we survey already have a finalised showroom or designer plan, and others are still at the idea stage. Either way, we measure the room, check waste and supply, and confirm what's structurally possible before any quote is written.

faqs.q: How far is Gerrards Cross from your base, and does that affect survey availability?
faqs.a: Gerrards Cross is around 25 to 30 minutes by road from our base in Bracknell, which means it's a normal part of our working area rather than a special arrangement. We schedule surveys there on the same basis as anywhere else we work.

faqs.q: What happens if the survey finds a problem with the waste run or access?
faqs.a: We tell you at the survey, not partway through the job. If a waste run needs moving or a doorway needs widening for level access, that's scoped and priced into the written quote you receive, so there are no surprises once fitting starts.

faqs.q: Can you survey a property if I've already chosen my bathroom brand and products?
faqs.a: Yes. We fit only, so a lot of the Gerrards Cross properties we survey already have sanitaryware, brassware or tiles chosen through a showroom or designer. We check the room against that specification and confirm what it means for the installation.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Gerrards Cross bathroom survey page, depicting the pre-installation measuring visit. Subject and action: a spirit level laid flat across a stripped timber floor beside an open notebook with a hand-sketched layout and a retractable tape measure extended toward a waste pipe stub, mid-survey rather than mid-build. Setting and work-stage: a mid-sized, part-stripped family bathroom in a substantial commuter-village house in Gerrards Cross, plasterboard partially removed to reveal studwork, daytime, cool overcast daylight through a frosted window. Composition: angled view from a kneeling height looking across the floor toward the window, tape measure and notebook filling the foreground, exposed studwork and waste stub visible in the mid-ground, window light at the back of the frame. Light and materials: flat, cool daylight through a frosted obscure-glass window mixing with a single handheld torch propped against the skirting board, bare chipboard subfloor, exposed timber stud partition, a copper waste pipe stub visible at floor level, uneven shadow falloff rather than even ambient light. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on fixtures, no LED strip lighting anywhere in frame, no catalog-symmetrical staging, no uniform gold colour wash, no plants or candles as styling props, no running water, varied and believable surface sheen with visible wear on the exposed stud and subfloor.
image.heroAlt: A spirit level and hand-sketched floor plan laid out during a bathroom survey in a part-stripped family bathroom in Gerrards Cross, exposed studwork and a copper waste stub visible under cool daylight.
